NO. 008 · Wetlands & Waterways / Ardeidae · Herons & Egrets

Chinese Pond Heron

池鹭 · chí lù Ardeola bacchus
Summer visitor / partly resident Abundant 42–52 cm Protected (China) IUCN LC

A camouflaged paddy hunter that only shows its white wings in flight

Standing at the edge of a wet field it is an unremarkable brown lump, capable of staring at the water without moving for ten minutes. The moment it takes off, a whole pair of snow-white wings snaps open — that contrast is one of the classic sights of the Delta's paddies.

Gallery

One scientific illustration for shape and colour blocks, two field photographs for how it looks in real light. Click any image to enlarge.

Identification

  • Breeding plumageHead, neck and breast chestnut, back blackish blue, wings and tail white — so vivid it looks like another species.
  • Non-breeding plumageEntirely brown, heavily streaked dark on head, neck and breast; it looks like the mud it stands on.
  • WingsIn every season the coverts and flight feathers are pure white and contrast hard with the brown body in flight — the master key to the species.
  • ShapeStocky, with a short neck (far shorter than a Little Egret), a yellow bill with a dark tip, and orange-yellow to yellow-green legs.

Behaviour

A classic ambush feeder: motionless at the edge of shallow water with the neck folded into an S, then a sudden stab at fish, shrimp, frogs or aquatic insects. Usually alone or in small parties; nests colonially in bamboo, mangrove or trees, often alongside other herons. Mostly a summer visitor here, though some stay all year.

Voice

Recording iNaturalist user lava_chen · Licence CC BY-NC · Original file

Usually silent; a harsh 'kraak' or 'gwaak' when flushed, short and unmusical. Low croaking around the colony in the breeding season.

Where to find it in Zhuhai

  • Doumen paddyfields
  • Jinwan fish ponds
  • Hengqin Mangzhou Wetland
  • Qi'ao Island gei wai
Field note
A brown, stubby heron staring into space is not yet identified — wait for it to fly. Pure white wings means Chinese Pond Heron; brown wings means a bittern.
